**A recurrence can be viewed as a structured matrix mapping past inputs to current outputs.** Its entries are constrained by the state transitions, unlike the freely input-dependent pairwise weights of ordinary softmax attention. Mamba-2's state-space duality uses this structure to connect recurrent computation with efficient matrix operations. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21060)

Chunk the sequence. Compute substantial within-chunk work with regular matrix multiplication, propagate a compact boundary state between chunks, and combine cross-chunk contributions. This exposes hardware-friendly operations without discarding the structured state-space model.

**The efficiency comes from exploiting structure.** Materializing a full dense sequence matrix would lose the intended savings. During decoding, a fixed-size recurrent state remains useful, while training can exploit parallel chunk operations.

Choose state and chunk sizes with numerical stability, memory, and throughput in mind. The model is not secretly ordinary softmax attention; its representational constraints differ. Evaluate retrieval and reasoning quality alongside kernel utilization. An algorithm that suits Tensor Cores is valuable only if the resulting model also captures the dependencies required by the task.

**Technical details and references.**

A state-space recurrence produces a structured sequence mixing matrix whose entries factor through transitions between time steps. In Mamba-2's SSD formulation, this semiseparable structure connects recurrent state updates with masked matrix operations. Chunking the sequence allows efficient within-chunk matrix multiplication, compact propagation of boundary states, and cross-chunk contributions. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21060)

This exposes large regular operations suited to Tensor Cores while retaining a fixed-size recurrent state for decoding. It does not turn the model into ordinary softmax attention: the structured mixing imposes different representational constraints. Compare sequence length, state size, chunk size, numerical stability, and hardware utilization. The benefit is an algorithm/hardware match, not simply replacing every recurrence with a dense quadratic matrix and hoping a faster kernel offsets the extra work.
